taste.name: Departure-board voice over shop-counter voice
taste.trigger: When choosing how every label, heading, row and button should sound and look
taste.decision: Chose one condensed family (Barlow Condensed + Semi Condensed) set in uppercase with 0.08-0.1em tracking for every non-paragraph role over a sentence-case pairing where headings and actions read like normal speech
taste.reason: Uppercase tracked condensed type reads as signage: it makes the page feel like an operations board that is already running. The cost is that a person scanning on a phone reads uppercase tracked text letter by letter, so the voice sounds like a machine announcing rather than someone explaining
evidence: 12px/600 uppercase 1.2px on buttons, nav, board rows, captions (12px = 116 uses, most frequent size)
only body paragraphs (14px #B6BBC2) and pricing bullets are sentence case

taste.name: One board component carries the whole story
taste.trigger: When each section needed something to show next to its heading
taste.decision: Chose to reuse the same bordered board panel (#1B1B1E, 4px radius, hairline rows, status cell flush right) for the method, the flow, the approval and the onboarding sections over a different visual per section (product screenshots, diagrams, photos of a real shop)
taste.reason: Repeating the board teaches the product's core object once and keeps the metaphor intact from top to bottom. It also means every section has the same silhouette (uppercase heading, small gray paragraph, full-width table), so after the second section the eye stops finding anything new
evidence: 4 of 6 content sections end in a full-width board panel (method 3 rows, flow 6 rows, approval 1 row, onboarding 3 rows)
FAQ is a 9-row bordered list of the same shape
single shadow 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.4) on board panels only

taste.name: Amber is the lamp for a human decision
taste.trigger: When deciding where the only warm color on a near-black page goes
taste.decision: Chose to reserve #FFB400 for the moments that need a person (the TU DECIDES line, the FALTA TU OK status, the Aprobar button, the primary CTA, the EMPEZAMOS AQUI step) and give machine-finished work a small green LISTO over spreading the accent across headings, icons and section backgrounds
taste.reason: When a single warm color appears only where the owner has to act, the page can say 'you stay in control' without a sentence: the eye goes to the amber, and the amber always means you. The rule breaks where amber also outlines date badges (LANZA Q3 2026, BAJO ACUERDO) that ask nothing of the reader
evidence: #4ADE80 only on LISTO cells and check marks
amber outline also on three pricing badges and the Negocio card border

taste.name: No pictures, no people, no numbers
taste.trigger: When the page needed proof that the product is real and for someone like the reader
taste.decision: Chose simulated board rows, each captioned as an example, as the only proof over product screenshots, photos of businesses, customer logos or metric counters
taste.reason: With no real testimonials or metrics yet, invented ones would be a lie, and the captions say so openly. The trade is that a small-business owner never sees a face, a shop, a phone screen or a price, so nothing on the page looks like their own day
evidence: captions 'Tablero de ejemplo. Tus filas son las tuyas.' and 'Un ejemplo funcional. Nada aquí es un registro de cliente.'
price headlines are GRATIS (beta) and A MEDIDA twice, no currency amount
no photo, illustration or screenshot anywhere in 5389px

baseline_friction: Mobile first screen leads with 'LOS AGENTES TRABAJAN': the subject is the machine, not the owner's business; the method sentence that explains the value is 14px #B6BBC2 below it
Uppercase tracked condensed type on almost every non-paragraph element; 12px is the most used size (116) and buttons are 12px caps

Jargon on a page for non-technical owners: ERP, CRM, RPA, agentes, lead, back office, embudo, atribución, Workforce, Brains, Pulse, Gateway dedicado o self-hosted, módulos, conectores, GitHub/Contribuir; the <title> says 'El ERP nativo para agentes'
Section monotony: every section is left-aligned uppercase h2 + ~440px gray paragraph + full-width bordered table; right ~55-65% of the 1280px container is empty beside each heading

Primary action has six names: Empezar, Recibe tu plan, Consigue tu plan gratis, Entrar a la beta, Hablemos, Escríbenos por WhatsApp; four middle sections have no real CTA while the approval demo shows fake Aprobar/Rechazar buttons
Pricing does not answer 'how much': GRATIS (Lanza Q3 2026, stale on 2026-10-24) and A MEDIDA twice; FAQ asks about 'plan empresarial' and 'plan miembros', names that match no card
Touch targets ~36px tall at 390px for both hero CTAs, below the 44px common minimum
Split-flap seam line crosses the FALTA TU OK cell, so at a glance it resembles the struck-through ANULADO row
8.7 phone screens long with ~60px between sections and no image to rest the eye
keep: Method section: plain-language step titles (Ordena el negocio / Ordena tus clientes / Automatiza lo que ya funciona) with ERP/CRM/RPA demoted to 12px right-aligned tags and EMPEZAMOS AQUI / DESPUÉS / LUEGO chips
Nada toca el dinero sin ti: one concrete approval card in local currency (S/ 240 against a S/ 200 limit) where amber = your decision
Honest example captions, AA-passing contrast (tertiary #8D939B at 5.9:1), focus-visible and prefers-reduced-motion respected
